title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Google Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Covers Google Cloud (IAM, API Keys, Cloud Storage). Covers Google Cloud project/org credentials; org policy constraints and VPC Service Controls need an organization resource; Workspace user OAuth and domain-wide delegation are in the separate `google` platform.

controls.name: Disable service account (serviceAccounts.disable)
controls.what: Immediately disables the SA, which is the documented way to cut off already-issued short-lived tokens.

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders
controls.what: Allow-lists which external IdP issuers can be configured.

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolAwsAccounts
controls.what: Allow-lists which AWS accounts can federate.

controls.name: Attribute conditions
controls.what: CEL condition on the provider limits which external tokens (e.g. which GitHub org) can be exchanged.

controls.name: Disable / delete workload identity pool
controls.what: Disabling or deleting the pool stops its identities from accessing Google Cloud.
controls.setting: IAM > Workload Identity Pools > Status toggle / Delete

controls.name: VPC Service Controls
controls.what: Service perimeters with ingress rules limit API access by network origin and identity, even with stolen credentials.

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders (Deny All)
controls.what: Org policy rule set to Deny All blocks creating new workload identity pool providers; exceptions can allow trusted providers per project. Same constraint as the existing limit_scope entry, used as a block.

controls_unknown: Whether existing keys created before iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours was set get an expiry (docs say 'newly created').
Whether API keys support an expiry setting.
Which audit field identifies the API key or HMAC access ID used on a data-plane request.
Whether GetKeyString/lookupKey calls are logged for keys.lookupKey.
Plan/pricing for VPC Service Controls (needs organization).

authentication.summary: An external workload (AWS, Azure, GitHub, other OIDC/SAML IdP) sends its IdP token to the Security Token Service and gets a federated token, used directly on resources or to impersonate a service account.

federation.details: Trust is based on the external IdP token plus provider attribute conditions; no Google user SSO is involved.

ip_restriction.boundary: VPC Service Controls perimeters only; no IP setting on the pool itself was found.

lifetime.summary: Federated bearer tokens valid up to 1 hour

renewal.expiry_basis: New exchange with a fresh external IdP token

administration.summary: Org policy allow-lists IdP issuers and AWS accounts; pools/providers can be disabled or deleted; attribute conditions restrict which external identities can exchange.
administration.conditions: Org policies need an organization resource.

offboard.details: Credentials come from external workloads' federated identities, not Google user accounts.

inventory.details: Pools and providers are listable org-wide in Cloud Asset Inventory; issued federated tokens are not.

inventory.ui: IAM & Admin > Workload Identity Federation (Workload Identity Pools page); org-wide: Asset Inventory search for iam.googleapis.com/WorkloadIdentityPool and WorkloadIdentityPoolProvider
inventory.cli: gcloud iam workload-identity-pools list --location=global; gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers list --workload-identity-pool=POOL --location=global

disable.ui: Organization policies > constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders > Manage policy (Deny all or list allowed issuer URIs)

expiry.api: POST https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token returns expires_in (seconds until the federated token expires)

usage.ui: Enable Data Access for Security Token Service API (IAM & Admin > Audit Logs); Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="sts.googleapis.com" protoPayload.methodName="google.identity.sts.v1.SecurityTokenService.ExchangeToken", read principalSubject

reads.ui: Enable Data Read for Cloud Storage (IAM & Admin > Audit Logs); Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="storage.googleapis.com", filter on the federated principal or impersonated SA

kill.ui: Workload Identity Pools > (pool) > Status toggle > Disable (provider: same on provider details); also disable any impersonated SA
kill.cli: gcloud iam workload-identity-pools update POOL --location=global --disabled; gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers update-oidc PROVIDER --workload-identity-pool=POOL --location=global --disabled

token_format.notes: Federated access token from STS; not documented as prefixed.

log_sources.name: Data Access logs for STS API and IAM API (Admin Read)
log_sources.notes: Must be enabled to log exchanges.

credential_id_fields.notes: External subject (AWS ARN, Azure object ID, OIDC sub)

anomaly_cues: Exchanges from unexpected GitHub org/repo or AWS account
Provider without attribute condition on a multi-tenant IdP

containment.steps: Disable the provider or pool; tighten attribute condition; disable impersonated SA to kill live tokens.
containment.notes: Disabling the pool blocks existing tokens (until re-enabled); disabling a provider only stops new exchanges and existing tokens keep working. Tokens from impersonated service accounts need separate action.

unknown: Whether disabling a pool invalidates tokens already issued

calls.reveals: Federated token for the external identity
calls.log_notes: Needs STS Admin Read Data Access logs

calls.reveals: Object names and metadata in a bucket
calls.log_notes: DATA_READ Data Access audit log; off by default.

unknown: Other calls same as gcp-2 after impersonation
